clue.text: Film king getting on bunk

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)
getting on means ageing, here in the spelling AGING
bunk is nonsense, and so is bull

explanation.surface: A monarch dozes off on a bed during a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but means nonsense, as BULL does.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging Bull is Martin Scorsese's 1980 boxing picture, so it is an example of a movie.

clue.text: Reckless forward, first to be dismissed

indicators.note: the opening letter of the synonym for forward is sent away, so it is dropped

parts.note: forward in the sense of cheeky or pushy is brash

explanation.surface: A careless striker in a cricket or football side is the first player sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to be dismissed' removes the B from BRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and reckless are synonyms: both describe acting without thought for consequences.

clue.text: MOD got mad with that woman sponsor

indicators.note: mad suggests letters gone wild, so the words MOD got are scrambled

parts.note: that woman is her

explanation.surface: A 1960s Mod became furious alongside a female backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns MODGOT into GODMOT; MOD is a 1960s British youth subculture.
explanation.definitionFit: A godmother stands as a sponsor for a child at its baptism, vouching for its religious upbringing.

clue.text: Some gen on étude, a musical composition

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some background information about a study piece describes a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece written for nine instruments or voices, a type of composition.

clue.text: Playwright sitting on top of retaining wall

indicators.note: in a down clue the playwright sits on, above, the next piece

parts.note: J. M. Barrie wrote Peter Pan

indicators.note: top of in a down clue picks the opening letter of retaining

explanation.surface: A dramatist perches on a retaining wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining wall' reads as one phrase, but 'retaining' only gives its first letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is any obstruction that blocks passage, which is what a wall does.

clue.text: Ball's lengthy dance

parts.note: lengthy means long
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A formal ball turns out to be a long dance evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance, but it is a cricket delivery. A LONG HOP in cricket is a short-pitched, easy-to-hit ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a long hop is a poor delivery bouncing short, a kind of bowled ball.

clue.text: Very long record, one beginning to chart

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of chart

explanation.surface: A lengthy single starts to climb the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective describes something of heroic scale or great length.

clue.text: Lose one's nerve parking? I can, unfortunately

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the words I can come out wrong, jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous driver frets about parking but insists they can manage.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic is to be seized by sudden fear, i.e. to lose composure.

clue.text: Miser, and the sort of fish they may like?

definitions.text: the sort of fish they may like?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., a low-priced fish of the ray family, which a stingy person would favour

explanation.surface: Wondering what fish a skinflint would order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person, so a miser; split, it is a cut-price ray.

clue.text: Irishman entertaining 500 in saloon

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the man's name holds the numeral within it

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An Irishman hosts five hundred people in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a bar but is the British word for a car body style.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon is the British term for the car body style Americans call a sedan.

clue.text: Protect receiver of stolen goods following call

indicators.note: following places the dealer after the telephone call

parts.note: to call on the telephone is to ring
a fence is a dealer in stolen property

explanation.surface: A stolen-goods dealer acts after a phone tip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money or assets is to guard them from being used elsewhere, so to shield them.

clue.text: Physicist's distant daughter taking place of wife

indicators.note: taking place of means one letter stands in where the other was

parts.note: distant means far away

explanation.surface: A scientist's estranged daughter has replaced his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking place of' swaps the W in FARAWAY for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Faraday was the English scientist who pioneered electromagnetism.

clue.text: Very large turkey to begin with, full-flavoured bird

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large

indicators.note: to begin with takes only the opening letter of turkey

parts.note: rich food is full-flavoured

explanation.surface: A huge, flavoursome turkey served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' suggests the bird; it only gives its initial T.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird, flightless and native to Africa.

clue.text: Go over playing field area quietly

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public playing field
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone walks across a sports field softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, i.e. revisit the main points.

clue.text: Rejects support after strikes

indicators.note: after puts the word for support behind the one for strikes

parts.note: strikes means knocks, as blows
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A union refuses to back its members following industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocks back is an informal phrasal verb for turns down or refuses.

clue.text: Last in Scottish Open, or out of form one who is never going to win?

definitions.text: one who is never going to win?

indicators.note: out of form means the letters lose their proper shape and are rearranged
Last in picks the closing letter of Scottish

explanation.surface: A golfer playing badly in the Scottish Open, the last in the field, has no chance of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of form' rearranges H with OPENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is a person or horse with no chance of success.

clue.text: Passageway in extremely pretty Scottish town

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
extremely picks the extreme letters of pretty, its first and last

parts.note: an aisle is a passageway between seats

explanation.surface: A walkway runs through a very attractive Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AISLE between P and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is a large town west of Glasgow, famous for its patterned shawls.

clue.text: Stuff cut in racecourse enclosure

parts.note: to pad is to stuff or fill
to dock is to cut short, as a tail or wages

explanation.surface: Padding sliced up inside a fenced area at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: The paddock is the area at a racecourse where horses are paraded before a race.

clue.text: Graves? One may know a lot about them

definitions.text: Graves? One may know a lot about them

parts.words: Graves? One may know a lot about them
parts.note: Graves is a Bordeaux wine region, so an expert on graves is a wine connoisseur rather than a gravedigger

explanation.surface: A question about who would be an authority on burial sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graves' suggests burial plots, but is a red or white wine from Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wine, so knows much about Graves vintages.

clue.text: Friendly drink

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means warm and friendly
a sweet fruit drink or liqueur

explanation.surface: A sociable beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm in manner, and also names a concentrated fruit syrup diluted to sip.

clue.text: Callas excited about American opera house

indicators.note: about puts the jumbled letters around the abbreviation
excited suggests the letters of Callas stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The diva Maria Callas is thrilled about an American opera venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges CALLAS, which then goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's most famous opera theatres.

clue.text: Boy, ten, worried about a blade

indicators.note: about places the jumbled letters around the single letter
worried suggests the words Boy and ten fretted out of order

explanation.surface: A ten-year-old boy frets over a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges BOYTEN into BYONET, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is the stabbing blade fixed to the muzzle of a rifle.

clue.text: Expresses dissatisfaction, reportedly at college drinking bout

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an unhappy crowd boos
being up is British usage for being in residence at a university

explanation.surface: A student grumbles about the drinking session at university.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOS said out loud is BOOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A booze-up is British slang for a heavy drinking party.

clue.text: Until now, like non-sparkling water?

explanation.surface: Is the water continuing flat?
explanation.definitionFit: Still means 'even now' and also describes flat water, as opposed to fizzy.

clue.text: To sleep in it is not appropriate

indicators.note: in places the word for sleep within the word it

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: A rule that dozing in it is not the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting, so is not appropriate.

clue.text: Bar opening as a temporary expedient

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: A pub opens as a makeshift measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary measure used until something better is found.

clue.text: Naive conservationist

explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced and also names an environmental campaigner.

clue.text: God Egyptian city upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: Suez is a port city in Egypt

explanation.surface: A deity is angered by an Egyptian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the king of the gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: A neat tray must be prepared, regardless

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of A neat tray are made into something new

explanation.surface: A tidy tray has to be got ready no matter what.
explanation.definitionFit: At any rate means in any case, so whatever happens.

clue.text: Best English, low in calories

parts.note: lite is a marketing spelling for light, meaning low in calories

explanation.surface: The finest English food is also low-fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best of a group, a select few at the top.

clue.text: Strip first of engines in aircraft

parts.note: a strip is a football team's kit, its uniform

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of engines

explanation.surface: Stripping out the first engine of a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like a verb, but a strip is a British football team's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite flies in the air, so it can loosely be called an aircraft; it is also RAF slang for a plane.

clue.text: More than one woodworker complains about log

indicators.note: about places the word for complaining around the word for log

parts.note: to carp is to complain
to log something is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a piece of firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log' suggests timber, but means record, ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpenters work with wood, so the plural answers several of them.
